original_value: Blockchain-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) systems have received extensive attention from academia and industry. Most previous constructions face the risk of leaking sensitive information since the servers can obtain plaintext data from the devices. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose a decentralized outsourcing computation (DOC) scheme, where the servers can perform fully homomorphic computations on encrypted data from the data owner according to the request of the data owner. In this process, the servers cannot obtain any plaintext data, and dishonest servers can be detected by the data owner. Then, we apply the DOC scheme in the IoT scenario to achieve a confidential blockchain-enabled IoT system, called BeeKeeper 2.0. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work in which servers of a blockchain-enabled IoT system can perform any-degree homomorphic multiplications and any number of additions on encrypted data from devices according to the requests of the devices without obtaining any plaintext data of the devices. Finally, we provide a detailed performance evaluation for the BeeKeeper 2.0 system by deploying it on Hyperledger Fabric and using Hyperledger Caliper for performance testing. According to our tests, the time consumed between the request stage and recover stage is no more than 3.3 s, which theoretically satisfies the production needs.

result.paraphrase: Blockchain-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) systems have attracted significant attention from both academia and industry. However, most existing constructions risk exposing sensitive information because servers can read plaintext data from devices. To solve this problem, we propose a decentralized outsourcing computation (DOC) scheme in which servers carry out fully homomorphic computations on encrypted data from the data owner based on the owner’s request. During this process, no plaintext data can be obtained by the servers, and the data owner can detect dishonest servers. We then adopt the DOC scheme in an IoT setting to build a confidential blockchain-enabled IoT system named BeeKeeper 2.0. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that enables servers in a blockchain-enabled IoT system to perform arbitrary-degree homomorphic multiplications and any number of additions on encrypted device data according to device requests, without learning any plaintext from the devices. Finally, we conduct a detailed performance evaluation of BeeKeeper 2.0 by deploying it on Hyperledger Fabric and testing it with Hyperledger Caliper. Our experiments show that the time from the request stage to the recover stage is no more than 3.3 s, which in theory meets production requirements.
